node-1.label: A 56-year-old man has a 3-month history of asymptomatic brown follicular hyperkeratotic plaques/papules spread across the body and significant hair loss on the scalp.

node-2.label: 56-year-old Japanese man; 3-month history of asymptomatic brown follicular hyperkeratotic plaque/papules spread across the body; significant hair loss on the scalp.

node-3.label: Some papules exhibited a comedo-like appearance and/or signs of infection; slight reduction in pubic and axillary hair growth.

node-4.label: Patient had been on dialysis for 3 years due to chronic renal failure.

node-5.label: No family history of similar conditions; no use of medications related to the symptoms; no exposure to dioxins; did not have COVID-19 and had not received any COVID-19 vaccines.

node-6.label: Blood and imaging tests showed normal blood dioxin and sex hormone levels, and no signs of malignancies or collagen diseases.

attrs.why: New expert analyses (pathologist and laboratory physician) describe biopsy findings of dilated infundibula, keratin plugs, lichenoid reaction, perifollicular fibrosis, follicular plugging, lichenoid infiltrate, and vacuolar alteration, which support acquired perforating disorder, especially with dialysis-dependent chronic renal failure. However, no explicit transepidermal elimination is identified and metabolic labs (calcium/phosphate/PTH/glucose) are pending, so the diagnosis remains leading but unconfirmed; confidence adjusted from 0.85 to 0.88.

Biopsy findings of dilated infundibula, keratin plugs, lichenoid reaction, and perifollicular fibrosis are more characteristic of acquired perforating disorder than of a simple follicular keratosis/alopecia. Normal dioxin and sex hormone levels, absent malignancy or collagen disease, and no culprit medications/COVID-19 further weaken this alternative. Confidence decreased from 0.15 to 0.08.
node-5 and node-6 directly refute exogenous/toxin cause: no dioxin exposure, normal dioxin levels, no related medications or COVID.
node-2 hair loss supports alopecia; node-6 normal sex hormones and no malignancy/collagen disease argue against endocrine/metabolic cause.

node-11.label: Skin biopsy shows dilated infundibula, keratin plugs, lichenoid reaction, and perifollicular fibrosis.

node-12.label: Skin biopsy shows follicular plugging, lichenoid infiltrate, and vacuolar alteration.

node-13.label: No explicit transepidermal elimination is identified on histology.
